newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-FIA DITCH PORTUGUESE GP, SWITCH RACE TO JEREZ.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FIA DITCH PORTUGUESE GP, SWITCH RACE TO JEREZ.

text.p: The last grand prix of the Formula One season has been switched to Jerez in Spain from Estoril due to uncertainties over work at the Portuguese Grand Prix venue, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) said on Thursday.

"Because of uncertainties as to the status of the work required at the Estoril circuit, the Grand Prix to be held on October 26 will take place at Jerez and will be known as the European Grand Prix," the FIA said in a statement.
"It is hoped that works at the Estoril circuit will be completed soon and that the Portuguese Grand Prix will re-appear on the World Championship calendar in the near future," it added.

Estoril and the French Grand Prix at Magny Cours, confirmed last month for June 29, were both included only conditionally in the provisional Formula One championship calendar in December. Estoril did, however, figure in the calendar issued in March.

Not normally the closing race of the season, the Portuguese Grand Prix had been scheduled last this year because engine makers Renault wanted to mark their last race in Formula One at a European venue.
The French race was confirmed after the organisers resolved a dispute over local television coverage.
